title: Stabilize Terraform module interfaces and introduce plan-snapshotting to reduce churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We have recurring terraform plan noise across multiple workspaces when small, non-functional changes to networking templates or provider defaults touch outputs and resource meta attributes. This creates incidental churn, stalls CI approvals, and makes automated rollouts noisy for Dedicated and Private customers.

Goal: Introduce a small compatibility layer and an explicit output contract for core networking modules (vpc, subnets, routing, nat) and implement a plan-snapshotting heuristic in CI that suppresses benign diffs. That should reduce false-positive plan failures, speed up PR reviews, and make provider upgrades safer.

Scope:
- Add a thin module interface wrapper (contract module) that re-exposes stable outputs (fixed names/types) for consumers and maps to underlying module internals.
- Remove environment-specific computed outputs from public interfaces; move them behind the contract module as local-only attributes.
- Implement plan-snapshotting in CI: capture last-applied-plan hash and only surface changes that are semantically significant (address, type, or configuration delta) using terraform plan -detailed-exitcode + json diff parsing.
- Upgrade AWS provider from 4.75 -> 5.3 in a separate, staged rollout with compatibility flags.
- Add CI gating: run a dry-run on a staging workspace using the plan-snapshot and a diff threshold; block merges that exceed threshold or contain provider-breaking changes.

Non-Goals: A full rewrite of all modules or changing runtime networking topology. This is focused on interface stability and CI ergonomics to reduce developer friction and accidental prod change risk.

Success metrics:
- Reduce number of PRs with incidental terraform plan noise by >= 70% within 6 weeks after rollout.
- Decrease average infra PR review time for networking changes from current baseline by 30%.
- No customer-facing infra incidents attributable to provider upgrade during staged rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Contract layer mapping may miss edge-case outputs used by a few repos. Mitigation: add automated inventory script to detect consumer references (grep across mono-repo / infra repos) and run compatibility tests in a compatibility matrix.
- Risk: Provider 5.x contains breaking behavior for a rare resource. Mitigation: staged upgrade (canary workspaces), smoke tests, and automated rollback path documented in runbook.

Rollout plan:
1) Inventory & audit (week 1): run inventory script, annotate consumers, open tiny follow-ups for outliers.
2) Contract module v0 (week 2): implement thin wrapper for vpc/subnet/nat with unit tests and examples.
3) CI plan-snapshot PoC (week 2): implement script that stores json plan + hash in S3 and gate thresholds in GitHub Actions.
4) Canary upgrade (week 3): upgrade provider in a small set of non-critical workspaces, exercise smoke tests.
5) Global rollout + monitoring (week 4-5): roll to all infra workspaces, monitor plan-noise metric and the infra-change-alert dashboard.
6) Cleanup (week 6): remove legacy outputs from modules and merge consumer changes.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Terraform+Module+Contract+and+Plan+Snapshotting
- Prototype PR (contract module): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/11234
- CI PoC (plan-snapshot): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-actions/pull/87
- Inventory script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/blob/main/bin/tf-output-inventory.sh

Next steps (this ticket): finish the contract module implementation and land the CI PoC in the infra-actions repository. Follow-ups tracked as sub-issues below.
